title: Onboarding Quant Audit — Perturbation & Slice Drift Notes Q1 2025
summary: Working notes from the first-pass quantization audit during model onboarding. Focus on slice-level perturbations across AWQ/GPTQ int4/int8 conversions and candidate mitigations.
body:
Context:
This doc captures early findings from the quantization impact audit for model candidate rwd-llama2-13B-v2 during onboarding. The goal is to identify slices with meaningful quality deltas when moving from fp16 to INT8/INT4 (both AWQ and GPTQ variants), prioritize follow-ups, and propose quick experiments to reduce regressions before granting 'serve-ready' status.

Datasets / prompt sets used:
- onboarding-promptset-v3 (1.5k examples) — mixed slices: code, math, longform-instruction, dialogue, multilingual (es/fr/zh), safety edgecases.
- internal-summaries-50k-subsample (200 examples) used for ROUGE/ROUGE-L checks.
- code-unit-tests (300 short problems) for functional correctness checks (compilation/run where applicable).
- human-eval-slicepack (100 multi-turn dialogs) used for subjective spot-checks.

Evaluation methodology (quick overview):
- Deterministic generation where applicable (fixed seeds) and sampling with top-p=0.95 for creativity slices.
- Metrics: task-specific accuracy/EM (math, code), ROUGE-L (summaries), BLEU (translation-ish), MRR for retrieval-style QAs, and a subjective quality score (human graded 1-5) for 120 hand-picked cases.
- Delta reporting: percent-point change versus fp16 baseline (fp16 -> quant variant). Slices considered notable if abs(delta) >= 1.2 percentage points or subjective delta >= 0.15 on 1-5 scale.

Results (high level):
- AWQ-INT8: Overall small aggregated loss vs fp16 (~0.8 pp). Majority of slices within noise, but the multilingual slice shows a -2.6 pp EM drop (es/zh examples) and a higher hallucination incidence in factoid queries.
- GPTQ-INT8: Comparable to AWQ-INT8 on average (~0.9 pp), but consistent pattern of minor tokenization artifacts on code outputs — truncated lines or missing closing braces in ~3% of code-unit-tests (vs 0.4% fp16).
- AWQ-INT4: Larger regression across longform (-4.3 pp ROUGE-L), math (-5.2 pp EM), and dialogue quality (subjective -0.42). Short answer Q/A less affected except for some numerics.
- GPTQ-INT4: Surprisingly slightly better than AWQ-INT4 on code (code correctness delta -1.1 pp vs -3.7 pp) but worse on multilingual (-6.1 pp EM).

Slice-level callouts (examples):
1) Math/chain-of-thought slice (150 examples)
   - fp16 EM: 68.7%  | AWQ-INT8: 66.5% (-2.2 pp) | GPTQ-INT8: 66.0% (-2.7 pp) | AWQ-INT4: 63.0% (-5.7 pp) | GPTQ-INT4: 62.1% (-6.6 pp)
   - Notes: INT4 variants frequently drop intermediate reasoning tokens; chain markers ("Step 1") are sometimes shortened leading to evaluation mismatches.

2) Code completion & correctness (300 examples)
   - fp16 correct run: 84.1% | AWQ-INT8: 82.9% (-1.2 pp) | GPTQ-INT8: 81.1% (-3.0 pp) | AWQ-INT4: 80.4% (-3.7 pp) | GPTQ-INT4: 83.0% (-1.1 pp)
   - Notes: GPTQ-INT4 appears to preserve token patterns for common language constructs but struggles on long multi-line functions; AWQ shows more whitespace/tokenization drift.

3) Multilingual translation/QA (200 examples across es/fr/zh)
   - fp16 EM: 71.4% | AWQ-INT8: 68.8% (-2.6 pp) | GPTQ-INT8: 68.1% (-3.3 pp) | AWQ-INT4: 64.0% (-7.4 pp) | GPTQ-INT4: 65.3% (-6.1 pp)
   - Notes: Subtoken quantization seems to disproportionately affect rarer subword embeddings -> increased OOV-like artifacts.

4) Longform summarization (100 examples)
   - fp16 ROUGE-L: 45.2 | AWQ-INT8: 44.0 (-1.2) | GPTQ-INT8: 43.8 (-1.4) | AWQ-INT4: 40.9 (-4.3) | GPTQ-INT4: 41.0 (-4.2)
   - Notes: Structural coherence drops in INT4: repeated clauses, omission of concluding sentences.

5) Safety / toxic edgecases (adversarial prompts)
   - Observed small increases in refusal failures for INT4 AWQ (~+2 cases / 200 prompts) where model returned semi-helpful but policy-risky text. GPTQ variants similar but noisier.

Hypotheses / root-cause signals observed:
- KV cache scaling: INT4 runs show more variance in attention normalization at longer contexts — correlates with longform and chain-of-thought regressions.
- Subtoken embedding shifts: Multilingual regressions align with tokens that are low-frequency in pretraining — quantization noise appears to push logits for rare subtokens across the decision boundary.
- Token alignment: AWQ path introduces more whitespace/token boundary artifacts (observed in code slice) possibly due to different rounding/scale handling in activation quantization.
- Calibration shift: Some temperature-like behavior changes (samples more or less likely to end early) — visible in truncated outputs.

Quick diagnostics we ran (notes):
- Per-layer activation drift snapshot (mean/var) between fp16 and quantized — layers 20-26 show highest KL drift for INT4.
- Attention-head sensitivity test: zeroed some heads and re-ran; tails more sensitive post-quantization (esp head indices 10, 15).
- Token-level logit heatmaps for multilingual examples to visualize decision boundary shifts.

Recommended next steps / experiments (priority ordering):
1) Short-term mitigations (low-effort):
   - For serving, enable hybrid precision for last 6 transformer blocks (keep fp16) for INT4 candidates and re-run critical slices. Targeted hybrid often recovers ~2–3 pp on affected slices in our quick checks. (Ticket: AM-4852)
   - Add simple post-processing heuristics for code outputs (auto-insert missing closing braces) for platform-level mitigation until quant behavior is stable.
2) Mid-term experiments (requires infra runs):
   - Re-evaluate AWQ scaling parameters (per-channel vs per-tensor) for embedding layers on multilingual data.
   - Run layer-wise quantization ablation to see if freezing quant on top-N layers helps chain-of-thought and longform coherence.
   - Explore KV-cache stabilization fixes (scale compensation) used in prior internal model optimizations.
3) Long-term / research items:
   - Propose a lightweight calibration dataset for multilingual rare-subtoken tuning pre-quantization. Could be added to onboarding checklist if effective.
   - Compare alternative quant backends (xformers-backed kernels) to isolate implementation differences between AWQ and GPTQ.

Action items / owners:
- Marcus: run hybrid-precision re-runs on AWQ-INT4 candidate for the mathematics slice (AM-4852) — due 2025-03-07.
- Ava: open a short PR with post-processing heuristics for code outputs (platform-level) and a lightweight canary (AM-4860).
- Tomás: coordinate layer-wise ablation experiments and upload per-layer activation drift plots to s3 (link in linked_artifacts).
- Me (Sofia): consolidate results into onboarding checklist and propose gating thresholds for INT8 vs INT4 serving readiness.

Open questions / discussion points:
- What is the acceptable delta threshold for subjective quality in longform — current internal bar is 0.2 on 1-5; should we make slice-specific bars?
- For hybrid-precision: what maximum extra memory/bandwidth budget can infra tolerate for Dedicated customers? Need SRE input.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc — numbers come from early mini-bench runs; not yet from full 10k evaluation pass. Please treat as actionable triage notes, not final gating decisions.
- If you want raw outputs or to replay experiments, see the s3 path in linked_artifacts.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Full 10k pass for onboarding-promptset-v3 across all quant backends (Marcus/Tomás)
- [ ] Add additional multilingual test cases for rare tokens (Ava)
- [ ] Draft recommended gating language for onboarding checklist PR (Sofia)

End of notes.
